webcpp::trystero::browser

The browser target: the backend interface over the page’s own WebSocket, RTCPeerConnection, RTCDataChannel, setTimeout and crypto.subtle, through emscripten::val. It needs a secure context (https, or http on localhost), where crypto.subtle exists.

Description

Tip: its objects, their handlers and the frames and texts they hand to the room are in the room’s resource; what emscripten::val holds is in the JavaScript heap, and the page’s event_loop keeps its registrations in its own resource.

Types

Name Description

backend

The browser’s factory: one per page, beside the page’s event_loop.

data_channel

A data channel over the page’s RTCDataChannel, its messages received as ArrayBuffer objects.

event_loop

The bridge between the page’s JavaScript event loop and an Asio io_context, which never runs on its own in a browser: it is polled after every JavaScript event that enters C++, and when work is posted from outside one.

executor

An Asio executor over an event_loop: what it is given runs on the loop’s io_context.

peer_connection

A peer connection over the page’s RTCPeerConnection.

sealer

AES-GCM through crypto.subtle, under a key imported once, as Trystero’s encrypt and decrypt do.

timer

A timer over the page’s setTimeout.

websocket

A WebSocket over the page’s WebSocket.

Functions

Name Description

depth

The function JavaScript calls, trystero_depth, before it enters C++ through trystero_dispatch: the depth trystero_recover restores if the call escapes.

dispatch

The one function JavaScript calls, trystero_dispatch, which browser/src.hpp exports.

recover

The function JavaScript calls, trystero_recover, when an exception escaped trystero_dispatch: the loop recovers, as event_loop::recover says.

operator==

Whether two executors are of one loop.

operator!=

Whether two executors are of different loops.

Using Declarations

Name Description

val

A JavaScript value, embind’s emscripten::val.

It makes each object in the memory resource the room gives it, room_config::memory: the objects, their handlers and registrations, and the frames and texts they hand to the room. What emscripten::val holds is in the JavaScript heap. It needs a secure context, where crypto.subtle exists.

webcpp::trystero::browser::backend::max_peer_connections

The most RTCPeerConnection objects the page’s rooms hold, every backend of the page together, counted from their construction until the garbage collector frees them: half of the 500 Chromium allows a page, which it counts the same way, so that a closed connection still counts until a collection the page cannot ask for.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/browser/backend.hpp>

inline constexpr static
std::size_t max_peer_connections = 256;

Description

Tip: a room makes at most 64 connections in any 57 s, so floods of four rooms reach this within a minute when no collection runs; the page then makes none until one does, and its rooms report each negotiation they cannot start, while the rest of Chromium’s count stays free for what the page makes without a room.

webcpp::trystero::browser::event_loop

The bridge between the page’s JavaScript event loop and an Asio io_context, which never runs on its own in a browser: it is polled after every JavaScript event that enters C++, and when work is posted from outside one.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/browser/event_loop.hpp>

class event_loop;

Description

JavaScript reaches C++ through handler(id, slot): a function bound to this loop, a registration and a slot, passed to trystero_dispatch (browser/src.hpp). An object registers a callback with add and removes it with remove when it is destroyed, so a late event for a destroyed object finds nothing. A loop must outlive the page’s use of it; its destructor marks every handler it made as dead.

Tip: a loop serves every room of the page, so the entries of its registrations are in the resource it is constructed with; a registered callback stays in its own allocator’s resource, a room’s for a room’s object, until it is removed or, for a promise, until the promise settles.

webcpp::trystero::browser::event_loop::recover

Brings the loop back after an exception escaped a call into C++ that entered at depth: the calls it unwound no longer count, and a poll runs the work that is ready.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/browser/event_loop.hpp>

void
recover(int depth);

Description

Tip: without WebAssembly exceptions no destructor runs while an exception unwinds, so the depth a call raised stays raised; the page’s function reads the depth before it enters C++ and gives it back here, so that a nested entry that escapes leaves the depth of the call still running below it, never less. The page’s function also puts WebAssembly’s stack pointer back where it was before the call, which no epilogue of the unwound frames did, but what those frames owned on the heap stays allocated: 312 bytes per escape, measured, for a frame that held a string of 300. With exceptions, trystero_dispatch catches a C++ exception itself, which frees it and runs every destructor, and recovers the same way.

Parameters

Name Description

depth

The depth when the call entered, as depth() read it; never below 0.

webcpp::trystero::native

The native target: the backend interface over libdatachannel for WebRTC, Boost.Beast for the relays’ WebSockets, OpenSSL for TLS and AES-GCM, and Asio for timers. Everything it reports runs on the executor it is given; the application runs that executor’s context, blocking on it or polling it.

Types

Name Description

backend

The native factory: one per application, beside the executor it runs on.

backend_config

What a native backend makes its peer connections with, beside the room’s room_config::ice_servers.

data_channel

A data channel of libdatachannel, the native RTCDataChannel.

peer_connection

A peer connection of libdatachannel, the native RTCPeerConnection, with its negotiation driven by the signaling.

sealer

AES-GCM under one room key, through OpenSSL, in Trystero’s sealed text form, what Trystero’s encrypt and decrypt do with crypto.subtle.

timer

An Asio timer whose waits are allocated in the room’s resource.

websocket_limits

What a native WebSocket tolerates of a relay that stops reading or answering.

Functions

Name Description

connect_websocket

Connects to a Nostr relay over Boost.Beast: ws:// in the clear, wss:// over TLS with tls.

webcpp::trystero::native::data_channel

A data channel of libdatachannel, the native RTCDataChannel.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/native/data_channel.hpp>

class data_channel
    : public backend::data_channel
    , public std::enable_shared_from_this<data_channel>

Description

Its events arrive on libdatachannel’s threads; each is posted to the executor and handled there, through a weak reference, so a late event for a destroyed channel does nothing. It exists only with exceptions: libdatachannel reports errors by throwing.

A text message, as a peer can send, or a binary one larger than any room frame (protocol::max_room_frame_bytes), is dropped on libdatachannel’s thread: neither can be a frame.

Tip: a received message is copied once, out of libdatachannel’s std::vector<std::byte> into the backend’s bytes, in the room’s resource, on the executor: what runs on libdatachannel’s threads touches no resource of the room, and its posts carry Asio’s default allocator.

webcpp::trystero::native::peer_connection

A peer connection of libdatachannel, the native RTCPeerConnection, with its negotiation driven by the signaling.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/native/peer_connection.hpp>

class peer_connection
    : public backend::peer_connection
    , public std::enable_shared_from_this<peer_connection>

Description

Automatic negotiation is off, so an offer or an answer exists only when set_local_description asks for one, as in the browser. It exists only with exceptions: libdatachannel reports errors by throwing.

| libdatachannel | Here | | events, on its own threads | posted to the executor, through a weak reference | | exceptions on refused input | error::backend_failure | | Candidate | the JSON of an RTCIceCandidateInit, as the browser writes it |

Tip: the connection, its handlers and the texts it hands to the room are in the room’s resource, and so are the rtc::PeerConnection object and its control block, which create makes with std::allocate_shared; what that object allocates inside libdatachannel, the data channels it creates, and the std::string and rtc::Description its API takes and returns, are libdatachannel’s.

webcpp::trystero::native::peer_connection::create

Makes a peer connection that gathers through servers, bound to bind_address when it is not empty.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/native/peer_connection.hpp>

static
std::shared_ptr<peer_connection>
create(
    boost::asio::any_io_executor ex,
    std::span<backend::ice_server const> servers,
    std::string_view bind_address,
    std::pmr::memory_resource* memory);

Description

A connection that is not bound gathers a host candidate on each interface but the loopback, which ICE never offers (RFC 8445, 5.1.1.1); one bound to an address, as "127.0.0.1", gathers on that address alone, which lets two peers of one machine connect with no other network.

bind_address

The local address it binds to, as "127.0.0.1"; empty means every interface but the loopback.

memory

The resource the connection, its handlers and its texts are allocated in.

webcpp::trystero::native::websocket_limits

What a native WebSocket tolerates of a relay that stops reading or answering.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/native/websocket.hpp>

struct websocket_limits;

Data Members

Name Description

idle_timeout

How long the connection may stay silent: half of it, a keep-alive ping is sent, and a relay that answers nothing within the whole of it is closed, which reports a close.

max_queued_bytes

The most bytes of text queued to write: a relay that stops reading lets them pile up, and a text beyond this drops the connection, which reports a close, so that the room reconnects with its backoff.

See Also

"The native backend", in the guide.

webcpp::trystero::native::websocket_limits::idle_timeout

How long the connection may stay silent: half of it, a keep-alive ping is sent, and a relay that answers nothing within the whole of it is closed, which reports a close.

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/native/websocket.hpp>

Description

It counts the bytes received, and a ping waits for the write in flight. Native only: a page’s WebSocket cannot ping, so the browser backend has no idle timeout.

webcpp::trystero::native::connect_websocket

Connects to a Nostr relay over Boost.Beast: ws:// in the clear, wss:// over TLS with tls.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/native/websocket.hpp>

std::shared_ptr<backend::websocket>
connect_websocket(
    boost::asio::any_io_executor const& ex,
    boost::asio::ssl::context& tls,
    std::string_view url,
    backend::websocket::handlers h,
    std::pmr::memory_resource* memory,
    websocket_limits limits = {});

Description

Writes are queued, one in flight at a time; a received message is handed over as a view of the read buffer, and one longer than protocol::max_relay_message_bytes closes the connection. A relay that stops reading is dropped once the queue would pass limits.max_queued_bytes, and one that stops answering once limits.idle_timeout passes with its keep-alive ping unanswered; both report a close. A URL it cannot parse reports a close, as an unreachable relay does. It needs no exceptions.

Return Value

The WebSocket; destroying it drops the connection without reporting it.

Parameters

Name Description

ex

The executor every handler runs on.

tls

The TLS context of wss://, which must outlive the connection and should verify peers.

url

The relay’s URL, read during the call.

h

What the WebSocket reports.

memory

The room’s resource, which the connection, its handlers and its queued texts are allocated in; Beast’s stream state and the coroutines’ frames are Asio’s.

limits

What it tolerates of a relay that stops reading or answering.

See Also

"The native backend", in the guide.

webcpp::trystero::protocol::json

Reading and writing the protocol’s JSON texts, with every allocation in the resource the caller gives. A text the protocol writes is a fixed shape of a few strings and numbers, so it is appended field by field rather than built as a boost::json::value, which would copy every string into a node of its own before serializing it again.

Description

Tip: strings are escaped by Boost.JSON’s serializer, so the bytes match what boost::json::serialize and JavaScript’s JSON.stringify write; a Nostr event id is a hash over exactly these bytes.

webcpp::trystero::protocol::frame_kind

The kind of an action frame, the low four bits of its second byte, in Trystero’s action wire, version 2.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/protocol/action_wire.hpp>

enum class frame_kind : uint8_t;

Description

A payload that fits one frame travels inline; a larger one is offered, accepted by the receiver, then sent in chunks. Integers and float64 values are big-endian, as DataView writes them.

| Frame | Bytes | | inline (kind 0) | 2, kind or format << 4, name (32 bytes, NUL padded), metadata length | | | (uint16), metadata, payload | | offer (kind 1) | the inline header, transfer id (uint32), payload size (float64), | | | metadata | | chunk (kind 2) | 2, 2, transfer id (uint32), offset (float64), bytes | | accepted (kind 3) | 2, 3, transfer id (uint32) | | rejected (kind 4) | 2, 4, transfer id (uint32), reason (UTF-8, at most 200 bytes) | | cancelled (kind 5) | 2, 5, transfer id (uint32) |

Members

Name Description

inline_payload

A whole payload, Trystero’s inline.

offer

The offer of a transfer, Trystero’s offer.

chunk

A piece of a transfer’s payload, Trystero’s chunk.

accepted

The receiver accepts an offer, Trystero’s accepted.

rejected

The receiver refuses an offer, Trystero’s rejected.

cancelled

The sender gives a transfer up, Trystero’s cancelled.

See Also

"The protocol", in the guide.

webcpp::trystero::action::async_send

Sends a message to options.targets, or every active peer, Trystero’s send.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/room.hpp>

template<class CompletionToken>
auto
async_send(
    T value,
    send_options options,
    CompletionToken&& token);

Description

A payload that fits one frame is sent inline; a larger one is offered, accepted by each receiver, and sent in chunks. Completes with (error_code) once each target’s local data channel has taken the inline frame, or the last chunk of a transfer the receiver accepted, as Trystero’s send resolves: nothing confirms that the receiver has the message. It completes with the first failure: error::invalid_action_name, error::metadata_too_large, error::no_such_peer, error::transfer_rejected, error::transfer_timed_out, error::channel_stalled, error::peer_disconnected or error::room_left.

Return Value

What the token’s initiation returns.

Template Parameters

Name Description

CompletionToken

An Asio completion token for void(error_code).

Parameters

Name Description

value

The message, taken at the call: moved when T owns its storage, copied once into the room’s resource when it is a view, and serialized at once into the room’s resource when it is a boost::json::value, or a payload that holds one.

options

The targets and the metadata.

token

The completion token.

A move-only callable of a signature, whose target is allocated through a memory resource; see the partial specialization handler<R(Args...)>.

class handler;

webcpp::trystero::handler<R(Args...)>

A move-only callable of the signature R(Args...), which holds its target inline when the target fits in three pointers and is nothrow-movable, and otherwise in storage of its allocator.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/handler.hpp>

template<
    class R,
    class... Args>
class handler<R(Args...)>;

Description

It replaces std::function wherever trystero keeps a handler (the backend’s, the room’s and its logger’s sink), since std::function takes no allocator since C++17. A room gives each handler it keeps its std::pmr::polymorphic_allocator<>, over room_config::memory; one constructed from a callable alone uses the default resource. The resource must outlive the handler.

Tip: a move assignment carries the source’s allocator with its target, as moving the target there does; the allocator-extended move, which a std::pmr container uses, moves the target into another resource when the two differ.

webcpp::trystero::room

A room joined over Trystero’s Nostr strategy, what Trystero’s joinRoom returns.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/room.hpp>

class room;

Description

Constructing it joins; async_leave leaves with Trystero’s farewell, and destroying it leaves at once. Its peers meet over the relays, connect over WebRTC and exchange the messages of the actions it makes, wire compatible with Trystero’s JavaScript.

Tip: every handler the room calls, and every completion, runs on the executor it was constructed with. The views a handler receives are valid for the duration of the call. Every allocation of the room goes through room_config::memory; a completion handler is allocated as its own associated allocator says. Destroying the room leaves operations pending on its executor, which free into that resource: it must outlive them (see room_config::memory).

Sets what is called with each problem with one peer that the room handled itself, as a wrong password or a timed-out handshake, Trystero’s onPeerError.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/room.hpp>

requires std::is_invocable_v<F&, std::string_view, boost::system::error_code,
                                     std::string_view>
void
on_error(F&& f);

Description

It is called too, with an empty peer id, for each part of the configuration the room dropped when it joined (error::invalid_configuration): a handler set right after the room is constructed sees those. Signals that do not open with the room key (error::wrong_password) are reported once per negotiation, and paced: the first of a quiet 10 s at once, with its peer, and the others of those 10 s in one report, with an empty peer id and a description that starts with their number, since anyone who reads the relays can send them from any number of fresh ids.

webcpp::trystero::room_config::memory

The resource every allocation of the room goes through, from its construction to its destruction; not null.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/room.hpp>

std::pmr::memory_resource* memory = std::pmr::get_default_resource();

Description

The room allocates there itself and all it holds: the copy of this configuration, its peers, actions, queues, frames, transfers, negotiations and relays, its handlers, the text it composes for its log, the objects its backend makes for it, the context libsecp256k1 signs with and the JSON it parses and writes. A message an action’s handler receives as a std::pmr::string, a pmr_bytes or a boost::json::value is there too; a completion handler is allocated as its own associated allocator says. What libdatachannel, OpenSSL and the browser’s JavaScript allocate stays theirs. The room uses the resource from its executor only, so it need not be thread-safe when that executor runs on one thread.

It must outlive the room, every value the room hands out (a std::pmr::string, a pmr_bytes, a boost::json::value), and every operation the room leaves pending: on Asio, until the io_context the room’s executor belongs to has run out of the room’s work or has been destroyed, so a resource is declared before its io_context; in the browser, until the room’s pending promises have settled. A room allocates and frees per event, so a resource that reuses what is freed (a pool) suits a long-lived room, and a monotonic one only a short-lived one.

See Also

"Allocation", in the guide.

Description

Empty means none: the signals are still sealed, under a key of the app and the room alone, as Trystero’s genKey does, and the handshake has no challenge.

webcpp::trystero::room_config::self_id

This peer’s id in the room, Trystero’s selfId; empty means 20 random characters.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/room.hpp>

std::pmr::string self_id = = {};

Description

Rooms of one app that meet a Trystero JS peer need ids of their own: Trystero keeps one connection per app and peer id, which all its rooms share, and drops a second one to the same id, while each room here makes its own. Given one id, two rooms meet a Trystero JS peer in one of them only; left empty, each room draws its own.

Other peers ignore an id longer than protocol::max_peer_id_bytes (64): the room replaces one with 20 random characters, and room::on_error reports it with error::invalid_configuration.

webcpp::trystero::error

What an operation of the library completes with when it does not succeed.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/error.hpp>

enum class error : int;

Description

Each value is one of the errors Trystero rejects a promise with or reports to onPeerError, as a code of error_category rather than a message: an operation completes with it, and room::on_error reports it with the peer it concerns.

Members

Name Description

room_left

The room was left while the operation was pending, Trystero’s "room left".

no_such_peer

The target is not an active peer of the room, Trystero’s "no active peer with id".

peer_disconnected

The peer went away before the operation finished, Trystero’s "peer disconnected".

invalid_action_name

The action’s name is not 1 to 32 UTF-8 bytes without NUL, as Trystero requires.

metadata_too_large

The action’s metadata does not fit one frame, Trystero’s "action metadata is too large".

transfer_rejected

The receiver refused a transfer, or a received payload is not of the awaited type.

transfer_timed_out

The receiver neither accepted nor refused a transfer in time.

channel_stalled

The data channel stopped draining while a transfer waited for it.

wrong_password

A peer’s signal or handshake used another password, or the peer sent a handshake message the protocol does not expect, Trystero’s "incorrect password for overlapping room".

handshake_timed_out

A connected peer did not finish the handshake in time, Trystero’s "handshake timed out".

handshake_failed

Reserved: nothing reports it today.

backend_failure

The browser or the native stack refused an operation.

invalid_configuration

The room’s configuration names something no backend can use, as an ICE server whose URL WebRTC refuses; the room goes on without it, and room::on_error reports it with no peer.

See Also

"Rooms and actions", in the guide.

WEBCPP_TRYSTERO_NO_EXCEPTIONS

Defined when trystero is built without exceptions: when webcpp has none (the compiler has none, or the developer defined WEBCPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS for every webcpp library), or when the developer defines it alone, to disable trystero’s in a build that has them.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/trystero/config.hpp>

#define WEBCPP_TRYSTERO_NO_EXCEPTIONS

Description

trystero raises no exception of its own: every operation that can fail completes with an error code. The native backend’s WebRTC, over libdatachannel, which reports errors by throwing, needs exceptions: while this is defined, native::data_channel, native::peer_connection and native::backend do not exist, and the rest of trystero is unchanged.

See Also

"The native backend", in the guide.

Appendix A: Differences from Trystero

trystero ports the part of Trystero 0.26.0 that rooms of messages need: the Nostr strategy, the signaling, the password handshake, the action wire and the room’s API. Where it keeps a feature, it keeps Trystero’s wire and its defaults; where it bounds what a peer or a relay can make a room hold, it says so in Bounded signaling, since Trystero JS bounds none of it. These features of Trystero are not ported, each for its reason:

Not ported Why

Audio and video: addStream, removeStream, addTrack, removeTrack, replaceTrack, onPeerStream and onPeerTrack, with the actions @_stream, @_track and @_signal and their renegotiation

The largest part left, on the roadmap (Roadmap): in the browser, the page’s MediaStream objects; natively, libdatachannel’s RTP tracks, whose capture, encoding and decoding would be the application’s. A room ignores a frame of one of these actions.

Request actions, kind: 'request': request, requestMany and onRequest

Not ported yet: an application answers a message with another, to its sender’s id.

onReceive, which accepts or declines an incoming transfer; the progress callbacks onProgress and onReceiveProgress; and cancelling a send with an AbortSignal

Not ported yet: a room accepts every transfer for an action with a receiver within max_receive_bytes, as Trystero does when no onReceive is set, and reports a transfer only when it completes.

onPeerHandshake, a handshake of the application’s own

Not ported yet: the password handshake, which runs on the same internal action, @_hsdata, is.

Passive rooms, passive: true

Not ported yet: a room always announces itself.

One connection shared by every room of an app between two peers

Not ported yet: each room makes its own connections, and ignores a frame that names another room’s token. So rooms of one app that meet a Trystero JS peer need peer ids of their own, which they draw by default (below).

The BitTorrent, MQTT, Firebase, Supabase, IPFS and WebSocket relay strategies

Each is a strategy of its own to port; Nostr’s public relays need no account and no server of the application’s own.

getRelaySockets, pauseRelayReconnection, resumeRelayReconnection, manualReconnection and warnOnRelayFailure

Not ported yet: a room reconnects with its backoff, and reports what its relays do through its log.

trickleIce: false, turnConfig and rtcPolyfill

Candidates are always trickled, as Trystero’s Nostr strategy does by default; ice_servers names every STUN and TURN server, in place of Trystero’s defaults; and the backend is what a polyfill would be.

Where a ported feature behaves otherwise

A peer id per room, not per app. Trystero’s selfId is one id for the whole page, and joinRoom returns the same room when it is called again for the same app and room. A room is an object of its own, with its own membership, connections and self_id, drawn for each room unless the configuration names one. Trystero keeps one connection per app and peer id, which all its rooms share, and drops a second connection to the same id. So two rooms of one app given the same self_id meet a Trystero JS peer in one of them only: the page drops the second room’s connection and sends that room’s frames over the first room’s, which the first room ignores. Given an id of its own each, or none, both rooms meet it, which the interop lane checks, natively and in the browser.

on_peer_join does not replay the joined peers. Trystero calls a newly assigned onPeerJoin with each peer already joined. A room reports a join from its executor, after the call that constructed it has returned, so a handler set right after the constructor sees every join; peers() lists the joined peers for a handler set later.

peers() lists ids. Trystero’s getPeers maps each id to its RTCPeerConnection. A connection is the backend’s, a page’s object in the browser and libdatachannel’s natively, and the room does not hand it out.

A send to a peer that has not joined fails. Trystero warns on the console and resolves; async_send completes with error::no_such_peer, since an operation that fails says so with its error code.

No example of trystero runs under the build, since each needs the public relays or a browser, so none has a twin in Trystero’s language, and the interop lane, not a twin, compares trystero with Trystero (The oracle and the interop lanes).

Appendix B: Roadmap

What trystero does not port yet, and what it does not build itself yet (Differences from Trystero gives each feature left out with its reason):

  1. Media. Audio and video tracks and streams, and Trystero’s @_stream, @_track and @_signal actions with renegotiation. In the browser they are the page’s MediaStreamTrack objects. Natively they would be libdatachannel’s RTP tracks, whose encoding, decoding and capture are the application’s. What that needs was measured: libdatachannel keeps only weak references to tracks, answers with every codec offered unless the answer is pruned, and echoes the offerer’s msid into the answer.

  2. Trystero’s other features. Request actions (kind: 'request'), decisions on incoming transfers and their progress, the application’s own handshake, passive rooms, one connection shared between several rooms of an app, and the other strategies, among them MQTT and BitTorrent trackers.

  3. The external libraries from webcpp’s own build. libsecp256k1, libdatachannel and OpenSSL are found where b2’s command line or the superproject’s .local/ says until webcpp builds them from third_party/ (Building).

Appendix C: Acknowledgements

trystero ports the wire protocol of Trystero 0.26.0, Copyright (c) 2021 Dan Motzenbecker, so that its rooms are Trystero’s rooms. It was written with Trystero’s source open: its protocol constants, its message layouts, its default relays in their order, with the shuffle that derives an app’s relays from its id, and its default STUN servers come from it. Trystero is distributed under the MIT License, whose text and copyright notice are in LICENSE-TRYSTERO.txt, at the root of the library, exactly as Trystero 0.26.0 ships them. That adds no licence to trystero’s own code, which is under the Boost Software License alone.

The BIP-340 signatures of the Nostr events are libsecp256k1's, by the Bitcoin Core contributors, under the MIT License. The native backend’s WebRTC is libdatachannel's, by Paul-Louis Ageneau, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0.
